idiom_name: conditional app.use('/path', mw) mount / stream.pipeline stage insertion
implementation_notes: In Express the route is the middleware array: mount the detour middleware with app.use only while the flag is set, so the message is inspected or tagged before it reaches the same handler, and let it call next() - that call is the rejoin. In stream-based flows the identical idea is an extra Transform added to stream.pipeline when the toggle is on, leaving source and destination untouched. Read the flag through a config provider rather than process.env at import time if operators must flip it without a redeploy.
pitfalls: A middleware mounted after the route declaration never runs for that route - mount the detour before the destination.
Reading process.env at module load makes the toggle deployment-time only; a live switch needs a request-time config or flag lookup.
Mutating req.body in the detour makes the legs non-equivalent for downstream consumers unless the change is additive and idempotent.
